fixture.src/slugkit/__init__.py:
"""Turn titles into URL slugs."""
import re
import unicodedata

__all__ = ["slugify"]


def slugify(text: str, sep: str = "-", max_length: int | None = None) -> str:
    """Lowercase, strip accents, and join words with sep. Truncates at a word boundary when max_length is set."""
    ascii_text = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text).encode("ascii", "ignore").decode()
    words = re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", ascii_text.lower())
    slug = sep.join(words)
    if max_length is not None and len(slug) > max_length:
        cut = slug[:max_length]
        slug = cut.rsplit(sep, 1)[0] if sep in cut else cut
    return slug

# Ledger API

Ledger API records double-entry transactions for the Acme finance team and exposes balances per account.

## Why double-entry

Every transfer writes two rows, a debit and a credit, in one database transaction. A balance is always the sum of its rows, so it can be recomputed from history and audited line by line. We chose this over storing running balances after the March 2025 reconciliation incident.

## Getting started

```sh
npm install
cp .env.example .env
npm run dev
```

## Configuration

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | Postgres connection string |
| `REDIS_URL` | Cache for balance lookups |

## Tests

```sh
npm test
```

# Gull

[![CI](https://github.com/acme/gull/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/acme/gull/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Gull steals your screenshots from Slack threads and files them in a folder, like a seagull with a filing habit.

## Why the name

Our first prototype ran on a laptop at the beach and a gull walked off with the sandwich next to it. The name stuck; the sandwich did not come back.

## Running it

```sh
npm install
npm run serve
```

Then open http://localhost:4000.

## FAQ

**Does it read my DMs?** No. It only sees channels you invite it to.

**Where do the files go?** Into `./gull-inbox`, one folder per channel.
